name: Slack Connector
description: Read and operate on Slack workspaces: list channels, read channel history and threads, search messages, look up users, post and reply to messages, react, pin and manage channels across multiple workspaces.

One message, with mentions and links already rendered readable.

params_schema.description:
The token the user pastes on the Connect screen.

tools.name: inbound_status
tools.description: Report whether the Slack events endpoint is ready: signing secret, endpoint URL, and what to paste into the Slack app settings.

params_schema.description: No inputs: it reports on configuration, which is not parameterised.
params_schema.title: InboundStatusParams

return_schema.description:
Whether Slack messages are reaching Webbee, and by which route.

Two separate facts, deliberately not collapsed into one. `ready` is about
PUSH (endpoint + signing secret); `aware` is about whether messages are
actually being recorded at all -- which the hourly sweep achieves without
push. Reporting only the first said "not ready" while awareness worked fine,
which is how a working feature gets debugged as a broken one.
return_schema.title: InboundStatus

tools.name: connect_events
tools.description: Save the Slack signing secret so inbound Slack events can be verified and accepted.

params_schema.description: Save the Slack signing secret that authenticates inbound deliveries.

signing_secret.description: The app's Signing Secret from Slack → Basic Information → App Credentials. A 32-character hex string; NOT the bot token.
signing_secret.title: Signing Secret

params_schema.title: ConnectEventsParams

return_schema.description:
Whether Slack messages are reaching Webbee, and by which route.

Two separate facts, deliberately not collapsed into one. `ready` is about
PUSH (endpoint + signing secret); `aware` is about whether messages are
actually being recorded at all -- which the hourly sweep achieves without
push. Reporting only the first said "not ready" while awareness worked fine,
which is how a working feature gets debugged as a broken one.
return_schema.title: InboundStatus

tools.name: catch_up
tools.description: Sweep every Slack conversation the app can reach -- channels it was added to and direct messages -- and record anything said since the last sweep. Use this to make Webbee aware of messages without waiting for push events.

params_schema.description:
Poll every reachable conversation and journal what is new.

This is the path that makes awareness work WITHOUT the inbound endpoint:
no signing secret, no automation slot, no platform fix. Slack is polled for
the conversations the app can read, and anything not already journalled is
recorded.

workspace.description: Workspace name, e.g. 'Acme'. Omit when only one Slack workspace is connected.
workspace.title: Workspace

limit_per_channel.description: How many recent messages to examine per conversation
limit_per_channel.title: Limit Per Channel

max_channels.description: How many conversations to sweep, at most
max_channels.title: Max Channels

include_channels.description: Sweep channels the app has been added to
include_channels.title: Include Channels

include_dms.description: Sweep direct messages with the app
include_dms.title: Include Dms

full.description: Ignore the saved position and re-examine recent history. Use after a gap; the journal still refuses duplicates.
full.title: Full

params_schema.title: CatchUpParams

return_schema.description: What one catch-up sweep looked at and what it newly learned.
return_schema.title: SweepReport

tools.name: list_inbound
tools.description: Show the Slack messages the app has recorded -- what was said, by whom, where, and whether it mentioned the app. Reads the journal; does not contact Slack.

params_schema.description:
Read what the journal remembers. Not WorkspaceScoped: the journal is
keyed by conversation, and a caller asking 'what came in' rarely knows or
cares which workspace a message belongs to.

limit.description: How many messages to return, newest first
limit.title: Limit

channel.description: Only this conversation, by name or id. Empty = all.
channel.title: Channel

unanswered_only.description: Only messages with no reply from the app yet
unanswered_only.title: Unanswered Only

params_schema.title: ListInboundParams

return_schema.description:
One journalled inbound message -- what was said, where, and by whom.

Carries `reply_thread_ts` because the whole point of remembering a message
is being able to answer it in the right place later, and re-deriving
Slack's thread rules at reply time is how replies end up in the wrong
thread.

Titled by TEXT for a concrete reason: the journal is how Webbee learns what
was said in Slack, and titling by author meant every row arrived in chat as
"Vladislav Ivanco" with the message body absent. The panel showed the words
(it renders the full record), chat did not -- so the same message was
visible in one surface and invisible in the other, and Webbee could not
mention what she could not read.
return_schema.title: InboundMessage

tools.name: join_channels
tools.description: Have the Slack app add itself to public channels, so it can see messages there. Names the channels, or joins every public channel it is not yet in. Private channels still need an invite from someone inside.

params_schema.description:
Have the app add ITSELF to public channels.

Exists because the alternative was a permanent chore: a human typing
/invite @app in every channel, including every channel created from now on.
A bot token with channels:join can join any PUBLIC channel unaided, so the
manual step was never actually required for the common case.

Private channels and DMs are untouched by this: Slack genuinely has no
self-join for a private channel (someone inside must invite), and a DM needs
no joining at all.

workspace.description: Workspace name, e.g. 'Acme'. Omit when only one Slack workspace is connected.
workspace.title: Workspace

channels.description: Channel names or ids, comma-separated, e.g. '#random, #lol-kek'. EMPTY joins every public channel the app can see but is not yet in.
channels.title: Channels

dry_run.description: List what would be joined without joining anything
dry_run.title: Dry Run

params_schema.title: JoinChannelsParams

return_schema.description: What the app joined, what it skipped, and what it could not do.
return_schema.title: JoinReport

secrets.name: slack_tokens
secrets.description: Slack app token(s) -- one per line, one line per workspace. Create an app at api.slack.com/apps, add the scopes you need, install it to the workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (starts with xoxb-).

secrets.name: slack_signing_secret
secrets.description: Slack signing secret — proves an inbound event really came from Slack. Find it at api.slack.com/apps → your app → Basic Information → App Credentials → Signing Secret. Needed only for inbound events; sending and reading work without it.
